why: PROMOTE. Facts from the raw request log, each backed by a claim below: (1) Zero errors - across all 9785 logged requests there were no 5xx and no non-200 responses on either version (stable 7374 requests, canary 2411). (2) Canary overall latency matches stable - canary p50 34 ms / p95 93 ms vs stable p50 34 ms / p95 94 ms, so canary p95 is within 5 ms of stable. (3) Per-endpoint p95 is within 5 ms of stable on all three endpoints (/browse 27 vs 27 ms, /search 59 vs 59 ms, /checkout 104 vs 103 ms). (4) Worst-case latency is not worse on the canary - the maximum observed latency is 339 ms on both stable and canary. (5) There is no regression over time - in each of the four 30 s windows the canary p95 stays within 10 ms of the stable p95 and both versions logged zero 5xx. (6) The one asymmetry is the canary /browse p99, which is higher than stable's (77 ms vs 28 ms), but no canary /browse request exceeded stable's worst /browse request (max 87 ms on both) and no canary /browse request exceeded 100 ms. Judgement: the /browse p99 gap is a tail-shape difference, not a new failure mode - the slow /browse requests on the canary are the same magnitude as the slow ones stable already serves, and the single canary pod has ~4x fewer samples per endpoint, so its tail percentile is far noisier. With zero errors, equal p50/p95 overall and per endpoint, no worse worst case, and no degradation in the final 30 s window, I see no customer-visible regression; blocking the release on a 1-pod p99 artifact is the worse trade. Judgement: promote, and keep watching /browse p99 after the rollout reaches 100% so a real tail regression would still be caught.

claims.query: (function(){var e=rows.filter(function(r){return r.status>=500}).length;var n=rows.filter(function(r){return r.status!==200}).length;print('C1 total='+rows.length+' stable='+stable.length+' canary='+canary.length+' 5xx='+e+' non200='+n);print('C1 VERDICT zero_errors '+(e===0&&n===0));})()

claims.claim: Canary overall latency matches stable: canary p50 34 ms / p95 93 ms vs stable p50 34 ms / p95 94 ms, so canary p95 is within 5 ms of stable.
claims.query: (function(){function P(a,p){var s=a.slice().sort(function(x,y){return x-y});var i=Math.min(s.length-1,Math.max(0,Math.ceil(p*s.length)-1));return s[i]}var S=stable.map(function(r){return r.ms}),C=canary.map(function(r){return r.ms});var sp=P(S,0.95),cp=P(C,0.95);print('C2 stable n='+S.length+' p50='+P(S,0.5)+' p95='+sp+' p99='+P(S,0.99));print('C2 canary n='+C.length+' p50='+P(C,0.5)+' p95='+cp+' p99='+P(C,0.99));print('C2 VERDICT canary_overall_p95_within_5ms '+((cp-sp)<=5));})()

claims.claim: Per-endpoint p95 is within 5 ms of stable on all three endpoints (/browse 27 vs 27 ms, /search 59 vs 59 ms, /checkout 104 vs 103 ms).
claims.query: (function(){function P(a,p){var s=a.slice().sort(function(x,y){return x-y});var i=Math.min(s.length-1,Math.max(0,Math.ceil(p*s.length)-1));return s[i]}var ok=true;['/browse','/search','/checkout'].forEach(function(pt){var S=stable.filter(function(r){return r.path===pt}).map(function(r){return r.ms});var C=canary.filter(function(r){return r.path===pt}).map(function(r){return r.ms});var d=P(C,0.95)-P(S,0.95);if(d>5)ok=false;print('C3 '+pt+' stable n='+S.length+' p50='+P(S,0.5)+' p95='+P(S,0.95)+' | canary n='+C.length+' p50='+P(C,0.5)+' p95='+P(C,0.95)+' diff_p95='+d);});print('C3 VERDICT all_paths_p95_within_5ms '+ok);})()
